confidence.rationale: Observed in Macro-Mission 02.1: historical tests wrote agent memory and shared learning files and restored them only afterward.

decision_rules: A test write is valid only when its destination is a temporary root or an explicitly injected sandbox.

evidence_refs.claim: The four historical writes and their call chains are identified and redirected.
Protected writes fail immediately and allowed writes remain below tmp_path.

failure_modes: A test changes a tracked memory, evidence, configuration, log, or product state file and relies on restoration after the run.

notes: Rollback remains recovery; it no longer substitutes for pre-write containment.

preconditions: Tests invoke persistence helpers or code paths with default repository roots.
procedure: Inject temporary persistence roots before test execution.
Block protected writes at the filesystem boundary.
Capture tracked-state status before and after the session.
Report path and caller when containment fails.
recovery: Stop the suite, isolate the writer, and rerun from the last clean checkpoint without destructive repository rollback.
stop_conditions: Do not call a restored repository clean evidence of no side effect.
Do not allow a test to write real product persistence as a fixture shortcut.
summary: Test persistence must be bounded before the write; post-run restoration is recovery evidence, not hermeticity evidence.
title: Test writes require a temporary boundary
validation: Debate and scoring flows pass with temporary stores and the tracked tree remains unchanged.
